parsed.basis: Banadir, centred on Mogadishu, inherits Somalia's criminalisation of same-sex conduct and gender nonconformity, with civil penalties of months to three years and severe societal stigma, no anti-discrimination protection, and regular prosecution in government-controlled areas. Unlike insurgent-controlled areas where capital punishment for alleged homosexual activity has been imposed, Banadir is under federal government control, hosts the national institutions, international missions and a more urban, cosmopolitan population, and has no documented local executions. That distance from insurgent rule is offset by pervasive security checkpoints, ID checks and conservative social norms that can forcibly out a visitor, limited recourse, and ongoing al-Shabaab infiltration and violence.
